result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers correctly say the page is in good shape and catch the one real defect: the `input` rule stretches the checkbox. B fixes it with a single minimal rule, marks the nav padding as optional and leaves the rest of the page alone. A adds several extra recommendations that are weak or partly invented: `tabindex="-1"` on `main`, turning the nav into a `ul`, and a `required` attribute. Its CSS also goes beyond the minimal fix, so it is the noisier answer. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers correctly find the one real bug: the checkbox picks up width:100% and padding from the input rule. A says plainly that the page is in good shape, names what already works, gives a minimal CSS fix and offers the nav padding as optional. B piles on extra suggestions that are mostly unnecessary. These are tabindex=-1 on main, a ul for the nav, required fields and a label class change. B also leans on a questionable target-size justification, which drifts toward inventing work.
